text:
The Dylan Larkin era in Detroit is over. After refusing to play until he was moved, the captain was traded to Montreal on Nov. 22 in a package NHL.com's headline said involved Kirby Dach and Michael Hage, and the Red Wings played their first game without him three nights later: a 5-1 win over Vancouver that the home crowd greeted with chants of "who needs Larkin." Sports Illustrated has Moritz Seider embracing "a new era." Detroit is 10-12-3, so the era starts from behind.

Our numbers say the hockey is a little better than the record and the scoring a lot worse. The Red Wings get 48.5% of the expected goals, close to even, but they have scored about 10 fewer goals than their chances deserve. Alex DeBrincat is the face of that: 2 points in his last 10 games on 8.3 expected. Goaltending has covered almost exactly the same amount at the other end, and Daniil Tarasov is .933 with 5.1 goals saved above expected over his last five starts.

The encouraging part is young. Emmitt Finnie had three points against Vancouver, and his line with DeBrincat and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard has 63% of the expected goals and an 8-1 goal edge in 81 minutes together.

Our numbers give Detroit a 16% chance at the playoffs after a 3-7-0 stretch. What we'd watch: how Todd McLellan rebuilds the middle of the lineup without Larkin, and whether DeBrincat's finishing comes back before the gap does.
